stemMd: In triangle $ABC$, the measure of angle $A$ is $34^\circ$ and the measure of angle $B$ is twice the measure of angle $A$. What is the measure, in degrees, of angle $C$?
instructionsMd: Student-produced response. Enter your answer in the box. Do not enter symbols such as a degree sign, percent sign, comma, or dollar sign.
explanationMd:
Find the second known angle, then use the fact that the three interior angles of a triangle sum to $180^\circ$.

Angle $B$ is twice angle $A$:

$$m\angle B = 2 \times 34^\circ = 68^\circ$$

Now subtract both known angles from $180^\circ$:

$$m\angle C = 180^\circ - 34^\circ - 68^\circ = 180^\circ - 102^\circ = 78^\circ$$

Angle $C$ measures $78$ degrees.

Check by adding all three back: $34 + 68 + 78 = 180$. If the three do not add to $180$, one of the two subtractions went wrong.

A sanity check on the shape: all three angles are under $90^\circ$, so this is an acute triangle, and angle $C$ is the largest of the three. In any triangle the largest angle faces the longest side, so side $AB$ must be the longest — a useful cross-check if a later part of a problem asks about side lengths.
accessibilityText: In triangle ABC, angle A measures 34 degrees and angle B is twice angle A. Find the measure of angle C in degrees. Enter a number without a degree sign.

provenance.notes: Original item. The angle measure was chosen so that both the doubling and the subtraction give whole numbers.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Angle B = 2 x 34 = 68. Angles sum to 180, so C = 180 - 34 - 68 = 78 degrees.

review.notes: Author solved and checked uniqueness: B = 68, C = 180 - 34 - 68 = 78, and 34 + 68 + 78 = 180. Awaiting a blind independent solve before publication.
